title: Task-demanded rank allocation in matrix memory
hypothesis: Per-task Mirror rank coordinates allocate only the effective rank demanded by each group-composition task, preserving heldout composition accuracy with fewer total bytes than a fixed-width matrix memory and outperforming native rank truncation.

world.task_composition: multiply two memory matrices and apply to heldout vectors
world.teacher: orthogonal rank-r perturbations around a shared identity memory

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed if native rank truncation matches or fixed/adaptive byte-quality gates fail.

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: composition nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer full bytes than fixed-rank memory, and strict quality/byte improvement over native rank truncation.
failure_gate: FAIL if native truncation exactly matches rank-code function or full byte frontier does not improve.
boundaries: Synthetic group-composition matrices only; no learned matrix memory or task-accuracy claim.
Task ranks are prescribed by construction; rank inference is not tested.
No fresh worlds after native control alias or gate failure.
